thread:
SecurityBot: ALERT: Unusual SSO activity detected -> rapid auth failures + session revokes across multiple regions. 1.2k failures in last 10m, ~3k session revokes. Possible credential-stuffing / automation. @Maya @Alex please triage. :warning:

Maya (sec): looking now. do we have geolocation spikes? could be impossible-travel pattern or just bot farms.

Alex (oncall): seeing concentrated spikes from three CIDR ranges that map to same ASN. lots of token_refresh failures with HTTP 401.

Sam (infra): can you paste the quick query you used? I'll prep temporary WAF blocks.

Alex (oncall): sure - running a quick auth-log query:
```
SELECT ip, region, event, count(*) as cnt
FROM sso_auth_logs
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '10 minutes'
AND event IN ('login_failed','session_revoked')
GROUP BY ip, region, event
ORDER BY cnt DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
Results: top IPs ~ 45% of fails, three regions: eu-west-1, us-east-1, ap-southeast-1.

Ellie (support): any user-facing sessions killed? Support queue just got 12 tickets claiming forced logout.

Maya (sec): we issued targeted session revokes for accounts with >5 fails in 5m and forced MFA re-enroll for 28 accounts flagged as high-risk. Notifying affected customers via support.

Sam (infra): WAF rule applied to block the three suspect CIDR ranges and rate-limit SSO endpoint to 5 req/s per IP. Also injected temporary RBAC restriction: service accounts used by internal automation cannot call /admin/sessions until we clear.

Ellie (support): acknowledged. Messaging draft for customers is ready, linking to status page. I’ll escalate for any org reporting mass impact.

Theo (legal): please capture timeline and affected customer count. We might need to notify depending on contractual requirements. Keep me updated on compromise evidence.

Maya (sec): quick forensics: no KMS key usage anomalies detected so far. SSO tokens appear to be brute-forced rather than cryptographic-signature-forged. Suggest delaying KMS rotation unless we find evidence of key exfiltration.

Alex (oncall): collecting audit log export now. Command I ran to pull last hour of auth events:
```
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /redwood/auth --start-time 2005000000 --filter-pattern "login_failed || session_revoked" > /tmp/auth_spike.json
```
Uploading to secure bucket for sec team.

Maya (sec): action items while triaging:
- preserve raw logs + snapshots (done by Alex)
- block offending CIDRs (Sam done)
- force MFA reset for flagged accounts (done)
- rotate any short-lived service creds if we see usage anomalies
- legal/comms loop (Theo & Ellie looped)

Maya (sec): short-term containment status: blocked ASN X, revoked ~3k sessions, rate-limits enforced. No confirmed key compromise.

Sam (infra): note: the temporary RBAC lock will impact internal CI that hits /admin/sessions for test users. I'll whitelist known CI IPs after verifying.

Ellie (support): sending customer notices now for 6 orgs that reported issues; generic status update for the rest.

Theo (legal): thanks. hold off on public disclosure until we have clearer impact numbers. If we confirm credential stuffing only, notification should be limited and factual.

Maya (sec): next steps / follow-ups:
- full postmortem draft (assigned to me) due EOD tomorrow
- add detection rule for cross-region simultaneous failures > 200/min
- add SSO provider integration test to catch replay/automation patterns
- evaluate KMS rotation if we find token signing anomalies
- review RBAC for admin endpoints (lock down by default)

Alex (oncall): I'll leave monitoring in high-alert for 24h and revert temp RBAC after Sam confirms CI whitelist.

SecurityBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: containment in place, monitoring continues. Priority: P2.

Maya (sec): thanks team. Will post postmortem link once draft is ready. If anyone finds evidence of token signing abuse, ping @Theo immediately. :lock:
